Assuage

uh-SWAYJ · verb

Hear It

What It Means

To assuage is to lessen the intensity of something.

A warm bath and a cup of tea did little to assuage her grief after the funeral.

Worked Example

The company's public apology helped assuage some of the customers' anger, though many still canceled their accounts.

The apology reduces -- but doesn't erase -- the intensity of the customers' feelings; assuage always implies lessening, not fully removing.

How Assuage Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

alleviate

alleviate: make less severe

mitigate

mitigate: make less severe or serious

Antonyms

aggravate

aggravate: make a problem or feeling worse

intensify

intensify: make stronger or more extreme

How Strong Is It? — ease → assuage → banish

ease vs. assuage

ease vs. assuage: To ease a feeling is a general, mild softening; to assuage it is to specifically lessen an intense, often painful feeling like grief or guilt.

banish vs. assuage

banish vs. assuage: Banish suggests completely getting rid of a feeling, going further than assuage, which only implies lessening its intensity.

Build the Word

The pieces

prefix — as-

prefix — as-: toward (Latin (ad-))

root — suag

root — suag: sweet, agreeable (Latin (suavis, via Old French))

suffix — -e

suffix — -e: verb-forming ending (English)

Put it together

Put it together: As- ('toward') plus a root related to suavis ('sweet, agreeable') plus the verb-forming -e gives roughly 'to make agreeable' -- to assuage a painful feeling is to make it more bearable.

Use the root in a new word: suave

Use the root in a new word: suave: Suave ('smoothly agreeable in manner') traces back to the same suavis root that likely lies behind assuage, though the connection is debated by etymologists.

Root Check

Word Choice

Assuage always implies lessening, never fully removing, an intense negative feeling -- grief, guilt, anger, or fear. Compare Allay (this same unit), which specifically targets fears and worries rather than any strong feeling in general.
